meta.titre: Chemical Composition of Food: elements, building units and energy values
meta.sous_theme: Carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and other nutrients

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Human Biology past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: In a market in Mbouda, a trader sells maize, beans and palm oil. Each of these foods gives the body something different: energy to run, material to grow, or a store for later. Behind these jobs is a difference in chemical makeup that can be written in a few lines. GCE questions often ask you to compare the three main classes of food, giving elements, building units, functions and examples, so a neat table in your head will earn many marks.

items: Food contains carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, vitamins, mineral salts, water and fibre.
Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen are chemical elements.
The unit of energy is the joule; one kilojoule (kJ) is 1000 joules.

sections.titre: Carbohydrates, proteins and lipids: makeup, units, functions and examples
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The three main classes

| Class | Elements | Building units | Examples | Main functions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Carbohydrates** | Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen (hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio 2 : 1, as in water) | Simple sugars (monosaccharides) such as glucose | Glucose, sucrose, starch, glycogen, cellulose | Main source of energy; storage (starch in plants, glycogen in liver and muscles); cellulose gives fibre |
| **Proteins** | Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, **nitrogen** (sometimes sulphur) | **Amino acids** (about 20 kinds) joined in long chains | Albumin (egg white), keratin, haemoglobin, enzymes | Growth and repair of cells; make enzymes, antibodies and some hormones |
| **Lipids** (fats and oils) | Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen (much less oxygen than carbohydrates) | One **glycerol** and three **fatty acids** | Palm oil, groundnut oil, butter | Energy store; insulation under the skin; protection of organs; carry fat-soluble vitamins; part of cell membranes |

### Answering "write short notes on..."
Take each class in turn and give four things: its elements, its building units, two functions and one example. Do not give tests and do not describe digestion unless asked.

### Energy
Gram for gram, lipids release a little more than twice as much energy as carbohydrates or proteins. When a question gives energy values per gram, multiply the mass of each nutrient by its value and add the results.

variantes.nom: Energy values on a food label
variantes.quand_utiliser: When masses of nutrients and energy values per gram are given
variantes.contenu_markdown: Energy of a nutrient (kJ) = mass (g) $\times$ energy value (kJ per g). Total energy is the sum for all nutrients. The share from one nutrient is $\frac{\text{energy from that nutrient}}{\text{total energy}} \times 100$. Always write the unit (kJ) and use the values given in the question.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked about the roles of the other nutrients or about an experiment with bone
variantes.contenu_markdown: Mineral salts are needed in small amounts: **calcium** hardens bones and teeth, **iron** is part of haemoglobin, and **iodine** is needed to make thyroxine. Vitamins are needed in small amounts for health. In bone, calcium salts give hardness and protein fibres give flexibility. Dilute acid dissolves the calcium salts, so an acid-treated bone becomes soft and bendable.

sections.enonce_markdown: A snack bar of mass 100 g contains 15 g of carbohydrate, 25 g of protein and 50 g of lipid. Use these energy values: carbohydrate 17 kJ per g, protein 17 kJ per g, lipid 37 kJ per g. Calculate the energy from each nutrient, the total energy, and the percentage of the energy that comes from lipid (1 decimal place). *(6 marks)*

etapes.justification: The energy values are given, so the method is multiplication, then addition, then a percentage.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Energy of a nutrient = mass $\times$ energy value per gram.

etapes.justification: Same method with the protein values.
Lipid has a higher value per gram.
Add the three results, then divide the lipid energy by the total.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The bar gives 255 kJ from carbohydrate, 425 kJ from protein and 1850 kJ from lipid, a total of **2530 kJ**. About **73.1%** of the energy comes from lipid, because the bar contains a large mass of lipid and lipid releases more energy per gram than the other nutrients.

items.pourquoi_faux: Carbohydrates have only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Nitrogen is the element that is always present in proteins.
items.correction_markdown: Carbohydrates: C, H, O. Proteins: C, H, O, N.

items.erreur_markdown: The building units of proteins are fatty acids.
items.pourquoi_faux: Fatty acids are units of lipids. Proteins are chains of amino acids.
items.correction_markdown: Proteins: amino acids. Lipids: glycerol and fatty acids. Carbohydrates: simple sugars.

items.erreur_markdown: Proteins are the main source of energy, so they are all that an athlete needs.
items.pourquoi_faux: The main energy source is carbohydrate; proteins are mostly used for growth and repair.
items.correction_markdown: Carbohydrates are the main energy source; proteins are for growth and repair, and lipids are a concentrated energy store.

items.erreur_markdown: Lipids have no function in the body except to make people fat.
items.pourquoi_faux: Lipids insulate the body, protect organs, carry fat-soluble vitamins and form part of the cell membranes.
items.correction_markdown: Give two or more clear functions, such as energy store and insulation.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Which class of food contains nitrogen? (b) Name the building units of lipids. (c) Give one example of a carbohydrate used for storage in plants and one used for storage in animals.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Proteins**. (b) **Glycerol and fatty acids** (one glycerol and three fatty acids). (c) Plants: **starch**; animals: **glycogen**.

items.enonce_markdown: A portion of food contains 30 g of carbohydrate, 10 g of protein and 5 g of lipid. Taking carbohydrate and protein as 17 kJ per g and lipid as 37 kJ per g, calculate (a) the energy from each nutrient, (b) the total energy and (c) the percentage of the energy that comes from lipid (1 decimal place).

A schoolgirl eats 300 g of a rice dish which is 25% carbohydrate by mass, and 150 g of fish which is 20% protein and 10% lipid by mass. Use 17 kJ per g for carbohydrate and protein and 37 kJ per g for lipid. (a) Calculate the energy she gets from the meal. (b) Her daily need is 9000 kJ. How much more energy must she get from other food? (c) What percentage of the meal's energy comes from the lipid in the fish (1 decimal place)? (d) State one function of the protein in the fish.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Carbohydrate in rice: $300 \times \frac{25}{100} = 75$ g, so $75 \times 17 = 1275$ kJ. Protein in fish: $150 \times \frac{20}{100} = 30$ g, so $30 \times 17 = 510$ kJ. Lipid in fish: $150 \times \frac{10}{100} = 15$ g, so $15 \times 37 = 555$ kJ. Total: $1275 + 510 + 555 =$ **2340 kJ**.

(b) $9000 - 2340 =$ **6660 kJ** more.

(c) $\frac{555}{2340} \times 100 =$ **23.7%**.

(d) Growth and repair of body cells (or making enzymes and antibodies).

items_markdown: Carbohydrates (C, H, O) are built from simple sugars and give energy; starch and glycogen are stores.
Proteins (C, H, O, N) are chains of amino acids and are used for growth, repair, enzymes and antibodies.
Lipids (C, H, O) are made of glycerol and fatty acids; they store energy, insulate and carry fat-soluble vitamins.
Energy = mass $\times$ energy value per gram; lipids release more energy per gram than carbohydrates or proteins.
Calcium hardens bone and acid removes it, leaving a soft bone. Use a neat table for notes on the three classes.
